title: First homework, then play: a first-then board
group: LDS-FOCUS — Focus and Getting Things Done
examples: How do I make myself do homework?
I want to play, not do homework

steps.label: First: homework
steps.note: Do the work, one bit at a time.

explain.say: Do you sometimes want to play, not do homework? Lots of people feel that way. Look at the board. It has just two boxes. First, and then. This is called a first-then board.

draw.text: First homework, then play: a first-then board

steps.label: First: homework
steps.note: Do the work, one bit at a time.

explain.say: See the pencil in the first box? First, homework. You do the work, one small bit at a time. You only think about this box right now. Can you say it with me? First, homework.

steps.label: First: homework
steps.note: Do the work, one bit at a time.

explain.say: Now look at the ball in the then box. Then, play. This is the fun part. It is waiting for you. Knowing it is coming helps you keep going. What fun thing would you put in your then box?

steps.label: First: homework
steps.note: Do the work, one bit at a time.

explain.say: When you feel stuck, look back at the board. You can say, First homework, then play. If the work is too hard, you can say, Can you help me, please? Asking is a smart thing to do.

steps.label: First: homework
steps.note: Do the work, one bit at a time.

explain.say: Homework done, so now it is play time. Brilliant, you did it! Here is a challenge. Make a first-then card for something tricky, like first teeth, then story. Try it tonight.

steps.label: First: homework
steps.note: Do the work, one bit at a time.

faq.a: It is a card with two boxes. The first box shows the job to do now. The then box shows the fun thing that comes after.
Something you enjoy, like playing outside, drawing, building blocks or a story. Choose it with a grown-up before you start.
asks: What goes in the then box?

faq.q: What if my homework is too hard?
faq.a: Do one small part, then stop and ask. You can say, Can you help me, please? A grown-up you trust can help.

faq.q: What if I really do not want to start?
faq.a: Look only at the first box. Do just one question. Starting is the hardest bit, and then it gets easier.
asks: I do not want to do it

faq.q: Can I use first-then for other things?
faq.a: Yes. First bath, then story. First shoes, then park. It works for any job that feels tricky.
asks: Where else can I use it?

facts: A first-then board has exactly two boxes: the job now and the reward next.
Many teachers use first-then boards to help children know what is coming.

quiz.say: On a first-then board, what goes in the first box?
quiz.show: What goes in the first box?
quiz.why: The first box shows the job you do now. The fun thing waits in the then box.

wrong.1: The fun thing comes after, in the then box.
wrong.2: The first box always shows a job to do.

quiz.say: First homework, then play. When do you play?
quiz.why: Play comes after homework is done. That is what then means.

wrong.0: Then means after, so play comes second.
wrong.2: You still do the homework first. Then you play.
